sites.tag_type: HA (also YFP, AP, V5 at same junction)
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed: HA-MDGA1 on COS7 cells bound soluble Nlg2-Fc (L3); surface HA signal quantified and used to normalize ligand binding (L4). Function validated: L9 explicitly states the tags were designed and confirmed not to alter protein folding, trafficking, or function, citing widespread dendritic/axonal localization matching untagged MDGA1. Endogenous HA-MDGA1 knock-in mice validated by Western blot (L10). MDGA1–neuroligin interaction preserved (L3).
sites.rationale: Python lookup confirms residue 18 = G (last residue of the 18-aa signal peptide MEVTCLLLLALIPFHCRG) and residue 19 = Q (first residue of the mature extracellular protein). L7 is the most explicit positional anchor: the donor oligo encodes HA-RSRD inserted after the signal sequence at the endogenous locus, confirmed by CRISPR knock-in. MDGA1 is GPI-anchored with no transmembrane helix, so the entire region 19–955 is extracellular and the distance-to-TM constraint is not limiting. All 12 ledger lines converge on this single junction; no other junction is named anywhere in the ledger. Multiple independent groups inserted HA, YFP, AP, and V5 tags immediately after the signal-peptide cleavage site (residue 18 / mature aa 19) of full-length, membrane-anchored rat or mouse MDGA1. L1/L11 subclone the mature coding region (aa 19–956) into spHA-C1 or spYFP-C1 vectors that prepend the tag before aa 19. L7 uses CRISPR/Cas9 HDR with a donor oligo encoding HA-RSRD flanked by 120 nt homology arms targeting the N-terminal coding region of the endogenous mouse Mdga1 locus, explicitly placing the tag after the signal sequence. L5 replaces the V5 tag of V5-MDGA1 with a 15 aa AP tag at the same N-terminal position.

sources.claim: Briefly, the gRNA to mouse Mdga1 gene (5’-CCCTTCCACTGTCGGGGACAAGG-3’), the donor oligo containing the HA-tag-RSRD linker (5’-TACCCATACGATGTTCCAGATTACGCTAGATCTCGAGAT-3’) flanked by 120 nt homology arms combined on both sides and Cas9 mRNA were coinjected into fertilized mouse eggs to generate targeted knock-in (KI) offspring.

literature_notes: All twelve ledger lines (L1–L12) describe tags placed at the same junction: immediately after the signal-peptide cleavage site, before the mature N-terminus at residue 19. No ledger line names any other junction, loop, or internal site for MDGA1. L2 (YFP, ~239 aa) and L5 (AP, 15 aa) and L12 (V5, 14 aa) confirm that tags of widely varying sizes are tolerated at this terminus, consistent with the GPI-anchored topology in which the entire ectodomain is free of transmembrane constraints. L3 and L4 provide surface-display evidence; L9 provides explicit functional validation. The rat construct numbering (aa 19–956) aligns with human canonical numbering (signal peptide 1–18, mature 19–955) with a one-residue difference in total length that does not affect the junction position. No intracellular sites, function-abrogating sites, or other non-surface positions were reported in the ledger.
